answer: A mailed sensory kit makes fakes costly. One single-use kit, posted to an address, is bound to the applicant's key: a numbered pigment swatch, a juniper scent strip, and a code card showing an oasis scene. Within 72 hours the applicant must pass a video check naming the pigment shade, identifying the juniper scent, and reading the code; the serial is then burned. Each fake costs $18 postage plus an 80 POA bond locked six epochs, slashed if a serial is shared, so cost scales linearly. Limits: postal delays, scent variation, resale; re-kit audits and serial revocation narrow the gaps.
